nodes.name: Fetch Due Carts
nodes.notes:
Due + active + not opted out, AND not a suppressed PHONE, LIMIT 50.

Was a GET on /carts until 2026-09-02. PostgREST cannot express "and this phone is not in another table", so the queue is now the case2_due_carts RPC, which carries the anti-join against case2_suppressions. Returns setof carts, so Prepare Cart Queue sees the same row shape it always did.

Why the queue and not a per-cart check: a customer who opts out may hold several carts, and may create NEW ones afterwards. Filtering at the queue is the only place that covers both without every future sender having to remember.

failed/undelivered => the touch is NOT counted.

Classifies the failure into three, not two (2026-09-03): terminal (the number cannot receive WhatsApp - close the cart), slow retry (a Meta or Twilio ceiling - back off 24h), or the ordinary +2h retry. Unrecognised codes retry, per locked decision #4.

touches_sent NOT incremented - the customer received nothing.

Same status + opted_out guard as the other cart writers (M5.2b, extended after chaos test 5.7). Without it this node RESURRECTS a cart that converted or opted out while the sweep was mid-send: it would re-arm next_touch_at +2h and overwrite the closed status back to abandoned/recovering. Found by reading the code after 5.7 - the first fix pass covered only two of this workflow's four cart writers.

The backoff is normally +2h, but Evaluate Delivery can ask for a longer one (2026-09-03). A per-user marketing frequency cap (131049) or our own daily account limit (63038) is a ceiling that will still be there in two hours, so those wait a full day instead of failing four more times first. TEST_MODE keeps the compressed backoff so the fast 3-touch regression still runs in minutes. The Evaluate Delivery read is wrapped in try/catch because this node is also reached from the Did Twilio Accept false branch, where no delivery poll ever ran.

- id: the cart
- touches_sent: optimistic lock against two overlapping sweeps double-incrementing

- opted_out=false: a STOP that landed mid-sweep must not be overwritten

parameters.content:
## 02 - Verifier & Touch Sender (the core)
Runs every 15 minutes. There are NO Wait nodes: every touch is a `next_touch_at` timestamp in
the `carts` table, and this sweep processes whatever is due (locked decision #1). That survives
n8n restarts, makes the queue visible in SQL, and lets a conversion or an opt-out cancel a
pending touch by simply nulling the timestamp.

Order per cart: verify against Shopify -> send-window/prayer gate -> generate -> send -> update.
The conversion check runs on EVERY sweep, immediately before the send, so a customer who bought
five minutes ago never receives a recovery message.

nodes.name: Note - Fail-safe: silence over a wrong message

parameters.content:
## Fail-safe: silence over a wrong message
Three outcomes, never two (locked decision #4):
- converted -> close the cart, no message, Slack the owner
- not_converted -> proven safe to send
- skip_api_failure -> UNKNOWN state: send nothing, leave next_touch_at alone, retry next sweep

Shopify answers HTTP 200 with an `errors` array when a scope is wrong, so "no orders found" and
"I was not allowed to look" are indistinguishable unless you check for `errors` explicitly.
Reading a permissions failure as "not converted" would message a customer who already paid.

nodes.name: Note - Send window + prayer gate (no Wait node)

parameters.content:
## Send window + prayer gate (no Wait node)
Case 1's logic, one behavioural change: instead of a Wait node holding the execution open, a
blocked cart has `next_touch_at` pushed forward to the window start and is picked up by a later
sweep.

Fallbacks matter here. A country with no `send_windows` row (a US shopper on a Gulf store) uses
the CART's timezone, not Asia/Dubai - otherwise New York inherits Gulf quiet hours and a Fri-Sat
weekend. If aladhan is unreachable the send proceeds: quiet hours already passed, and a missing
prayer calendar is not a reason to withhold a transactional message.

TEST_MODE (in `Set Sweep Config`) only changes the ACTION, never the calculation - the gate is
always computed and logged honestly, so a bypassed send still records what it would have done.

nodes.name: Note - 3-touch cap and the touch schedule

parameters.content:
## 3-touch cap and the touch schedule
touches_sent 1 -> +24h, 2 -> +48h, 3 -> next_touch_at NULL + status `exhausted` (spec 5).
There is no code path that can produce a 4th touch, and `carts.touches_sent` also carries a
CHECK (0..3) constraint so a future bug in this workflow still cannot message a customer again.

The PATCH filters on `touches_sent=eq.<value read at the start of this cart>`. If two sweeps
ever overlapped, the second update matches 0 rows instead of double-counting, and the run log
records `rows_updated: 0` rather than silently lying about the send.

A touch is counted only after Twilio confirms it did not FAIL. Twilio returns a SID at
acceptance, before delivery is attempted - on 2026-08-03 three messages came back `queued` and
later failed with 63015, each having already consumed one of the three permitted touches. The
Wait + re-read closes that. Cost: ~10s per cart, so a full 50-cart sweep takes ~8.5 min against
a 15-min cycle. Above roughly 80 due carts per sweep this must become a Twilio status-callback
webhook instead of a poll.

M5 decision (Hussein, 2026-08-04): the poll STAYS for this build. A status callback needs a
stable public URL, and this demo runs on a quick cloudflared tunnel that has died six times.
A delivery-confirmation mechanism that depends on the least reliable component in the stack is
worse than none. First thing to change on a real deployment with a real hostname.

nodes.name: Summarize Sweep
nodes.notes: Reads back THIS execution's own run_logs rows. Querying by execution_id rather than accumulating loop output is deliberate: every terminal branch of the loop returns a different item shape (HTTP responses from six different nodes), so counting them in code would be fragile. The log rows are already the canonical record - this just reads them.

nodes.name: Build Sweep Summary
nodes.notes:
ONE alert per sweep, never per cart: a Shopify outage across 50 due carts produces a single Slack message, not 50. Degraded = any failed row, any cart skipped on an unknown Shopify state, any Twilio send failure, a dead cart queue, or a run_logs read-back that itself failed.

A cart closed as undeliverable is counted but does NOT make the sweep degraded - a dead number is a campaign outcome, not a system fault.

nodes.name: Log Sweep Summary

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ workflow_name: '02 - Verifier & Touch Sender', execution_id: $execution.id, cart_id: null, status: $json.degraded ? 'partial' : 'success', step_name: 'sweep_summary', error_message: $json.degraded ? ('sweep degraded: ' + $json.slack_body.text).slice(0, 1000) : null, metadata: $json.summary }) }}

nodes.notes: One row per NON-EMPTY sweep. Empty sweeps never reach here (Prepare Cart Queue returns zero items, so nothing downstream executes) - the 'don't log 96 idle sweeps a day' decision from M3.1 still holds. This row is what the daily digest reads for sweep coverage.

nodes.name: Is Sweep Degraded
nodes.notes: True only when the sweep did not do its job cleanly. A clean sweep writes its summary row and stops here - silence in #automation-errors means the queue was drained without incident.

nodes.name: Alert Degraded Sweep
nodes.notes: Operational alert to #automation-errors (NOT #leads - that channel is for business events like a recovered order). Fills the gap the global error handler cannot: every degradation path in this sweep is Continue-On-Fail by design, so none of it ever crashes and none of it would otherwise be seen until the next morning's digest.

parameters.content:
## Sweep summary + degraded alert (M5.2b)
Every degradation path in this workflow is **Continue-On-Fail by design** - a Shopify outage skips carts, a Twilio failure postpones a touch, a closed window defers one. None of them crash, so **none of them ever reach `99 - Error Handler C2`**, which only fires on unhandled errors.

Without this block, a Shopify outage that skipped all 50 due carts would look exactly like a quiet afternoon until someone read `run_logs` or the 08:00 digest arrived.

`Summarize Sweep` re-reads this execution's own `run_logs` rows by `execution_id` (not by accumulating loop output - the six terminal branches all return different item shapes), writes ONE `sweep_summary` row, and alerts **#automation-errors** only when something actually went wrong.

**One alert per sweep, never per cart.** 50 skipped carts = 1 Slack message, not 50.

A `run_logs` read-back that itself fails counts as degraded: observability that cannot read itself must not report a clean sweep.

Empty sweeps still write nothing at all - `Prepare Cart Queue` returns zero items, so nothing downstream executes (M3.1: no 96 idle rows a day).

nodes.name: Note - Arabic enforced in code, not asked for

parameters.content:
## The Arabic register layer lives in `Parse Touch Message`

Register compliance is **probabilistic**: the same prompt and the same cart, 15 minutes apart, produced one rejected generation and one clean one. So anything mechanically checkable is enforced here, and a message that fails is replaced by the respectful static template with the reason recorded in `degrade_reason` — visible in `run_logs` and the daily digest rather than invisible.

**11 rules, all traceable to `prompts/arabic-style-guide.md`** (which derives from `arabic-master-reference.md` at the work root — Hussein owns both). Four of them exist because a wrong message was **delivered to a real handset** first.

**Gender-conditional since 2026-08-07:** the MSA feminine present (`تستخدمين`) is correct for a customer we know to be female and an error otherwise. The colloquial dropped-ن form (`تستخدمي`) is wrong for everyone. `customer_gender` comes from intake and is sticky.

**Deliberately high-precision, not exhaustive.** Over-matching would send every Arabic customer a template and silently delete the personalisation that is the point of the feature.

Run `tests/parse-touch-message.test.js` after ANY edit to this node, the prompt, or the style guide — it loads `jsCode` out of the export, so **re-export first**.

nodes.name: Route Send Failure
nodes.notes:
Terminal delivery failure (the number cannot receive WhatsApp) closes the cart; everything else keeps the retry it has always had.

Only reachable from Did Send Succeed, which means Evaluate Delivery has run. The Did Twilio Accept false branch bypasses this on purpose: no SID means no delivery information at all, so there is nothing to classify and the cart must be retried.

nodes.name: Close Undeliverable Cart
nodes.notes:
The number cannot receive WhatsApp, so stop: status undeliverable, schedule nulled, no further touches.

touches_sent is NOT incremented - the customer received nothing, and 'exhausted' would claim three delivered messages that never arrived.

Same status + opted_out guard as the other cart writers here. A cart that converted or opted out while this sweep was mid-send must not be overwritten to undeliverable; that PATCH matches 0 rows instead and the run log says so.

nodes.notes: Logged as SUCCESS, not failed, on purpose. A dead number is a normal outcome of running a recovery campaign, not a fault in this system, and marking it failed would flag every sweep that meets one as degraded and page the owner. It gets its own step_name and its own digest count instead, so it is visible without being an alarm.
